newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate's Daschle to back Republican tax bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate's Daschle to back Republican tax bill.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said he would vote for a Republican-crafted tax bill now under debate, despite concerns most of its benefits would flow to the wealthiest Americans.
"We don't want the perfect to be the enemy of the good. There are some good things in here," the South Dakota Democrat told reporters.
He said he hoped to work with the White House to improve on the measure in coming weeks when House and Senate negotiators met to work out a final, compromise bill.
The Senate is debating legislation to cut taxes by a net $77 billion over five years including a capital gains tax rate cut, education tax breaks and more liberal estate tax provisions.

Senate Democrats, led by Daschle, planned to offer an alternative five-year tax cut plan, despite the fact that Democrats on the Senate Finance Committee helped draft the bill under consideration and approved it last week.

The Democratic plan would exclude from taxation 30 percent of gains on investments such as stocks for people of all income levels. The Republican plan cuts the maximum individual capital gains tax rate to 20 percent from 28 percent.
Daschle said it was possible some Democrats on the Finance Committee would not support the alternative plan.
Daschle was joined at a news conference by House Democratic Leader Dick Gephardt, who plans to vote against a companion tax measure now moving through that chamber.
"Democrats are for cutting taxes for hard-working middle income families in this country," Gephardt said, also complaining the House bill would mainly benefit the wealthy.
He complained that Democrats were shut out of the process of crafting the House tax bill.
